data.body:
DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE — the key is never mounted INTO the container. My two earlier
diagnoses were both wrong; correcting the record.

WRONG #1: 'the SSM slot is unpopulated'. It is populated — /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key,
SecureString, 433 chars, OpenSSH private key, LastModified 2026-07-14T16:47Z.

WRONG #2: 'the host booted before the key existed, so restart it'. Disproved on the host:
fetch-secrets.sh has re-run (the .env and the key file are both stamped 2026-08-09 15:58) and
compose-review-bot-1 restarted ~15:43 today — yet events at 16:16 are still unsigned. A
restart does not and cannot fix this.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (verified over SSM on i-00880b2c7f13527c5):
  inside the container:  REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/opt/rebar/infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key
  that path inside:      ls: cannot access ... No such file or directory
  same path on the host: -rw------- 1 root root 432 Aug  9 15:58
  review-bot mounts:     gerrit_reviewbot -> /var/gerrit/site/reviewbot
                         gerrit_reviewbot_tickets -> /var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets
                         (no compose-dir bind mount, no key mount)

fetch-secrets.sh materializes the key to a HOST path and exports that HOST path into the
container through `env_file: - .env`. docker-compose.yml never bind-mounts the file, so the
variable points at a path that does not exist in the container's namespace. rebar reads the
var, cannot open the file, and silently falls back to unsigned. The env var being set is what
makes this invisible — every check short of opening the file passes.

FIX (code, not ops — no AWS-only action can resolve it):
  1. Bind-mount the key read-only into the review-bot service and set the CONTAINER-side path
     explicitly in the service `environment:` (overriding the host path inherited from
     env_file), e.g. ./rebar-bot-signing-key:/run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key:ro
  2. EDGE CASE: docker creates a DIRECTORY when bind-mounting a missing file. fetch-secrets.sh
     currently creates the file only when the SSM value is non-empty, so an unpopulated slot
     would break container start. Have fetch-secrets.sh always create the file (0600, possibly
     empty) so the mount is stable, and let an empty key mean unsigned.
  3. Make the failure LOUD: signing that is configured but unreadable should warn or fail,
     not silently downgrade — that silence is why this ran for a month.
